transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hey, yeah, nice to meet you too. Um, so I came in because I just... I feel like I’m literally crawling out of my skin whenever I’m supposed to sit still. Like, especially in the radiology suite at work, or in my classes. Actually, the chairs in my Tuesday lecture are those terrible plastic ones that are connected to the tiny desks? I don't know who designed those, but they're the worst. My buddy Josh tried to lean back in one last week and the whole thing just tipped over in the middle of a lecture. It was hilarious, the professor was so mad, he actually stopped the whole slideshow. But, uh, what was I saying? Right, so I've been trying to just tough it out for months now, just trying to sit normally, but I still just end up pacing around the control room, or shifting constantly, or finding literally any excuse to get up and move. I just can't stay put.
Did this feeling of needing to move start after you began a new medication or changed the dose of one?

Medication? Uh, no, I don't take anything. I mean, unless you count energy drinks? I had this phase a couple weeks ago where I was drinking those massive cans of Reign before my morning clinicals. The sour apple one is amazing, but it made my hands shake so bad when I was trying to position the X-ray tube. The lead tech, Brenda—she's been there for like thirty years—she actually snapped at me because I almost dropped a detector. Our backup portable machine is super old, it honestly looks like a literal washing machine on wheels. It’s so heavy to push down the hospital hallways, especially when the wheels get stuck on the elevator tracks. I always get the one with the bad wheel. But yeah, no, no prescription meds or dose changes or anything like that. I don't even take Tylenol most of the time.
Since childhood, have you often had trouble paying attention or staying focused?

Trouble paying attention? Um, not really, no. I mean, I can focus just fine on stuff. Like when I was a kid, I could spend hours building those massive Lego sets. I had the Death Star one, the huge one with like four thousand pieces? My mom actually found it at a garage sale, which is insane because those things go for hundreds of dollars online now. The guy selling it was just trying to clear out his garage, he had all these vintage records too. Like original pressing Beatles albums and stuff. I don't really listen to vinyl myself, but my roommate Dave does. He brought this giant record player to our dorm and it takes up literally half his desk, so he’s always complaining he has nowhere to put his laptop when he studies. He had to buy this weird little lap desk thing off Amazon, but it's super flimsy. But, uh... wait, what were we talking about? Focus? Yeah, no, I don't think I've ever really had a problem with that.
Have you been hearing voices when no one else is around?

Voices? Uh, no. Definitely not. I mean, the only thing I hear when it's quiet is just... regular stuff. Or like, the hum of the machines at the clinic. Seriously, the MRI machine is so loud, even from down the hall. It sounds like a broken washing machine mixed with a jackhammer. My buddy Josh actually tried to record it on his phone once to use as a sample for this music production class he's taking. He bought this massive synthesizer board last month with all these glowing buttons and sliders, it looks like a spaceship console. He spent like four hours on Sunday just hitting the exact same snare drum pad over and over while I was trying to study for my skull anatomy practical. It was driving me absolutely insane. I had to go sit in my car just to get away from the tapping. My car's AC is busted though, so it was like sitting in a literal sauna, and the cupholder is broken so I spilled my drink... but anyway, wait, voices? Yeah, no, no voices or anything like that.
Have you had times when you felt unusually energized or up for several days in a row?

Energized for several days? Um, no, not like days in a row. I mean, I'm always kind of bouncing off the walls a little bit, but it's not like a multi-day high or anything. Like, yesterday in my radiation safety lecture, I literally couldn't stop tapping my foot, but that's just normal for me. That class is so ridiculously boring anyway. The instructor, Mr. Davis, he always wears these crazy bright ties, right? Yesterday's had these little cartoon hotdogs all over it. Like, who even buys a hotdog tie? Probably from one of those joke shops at the mall. I haven't been to the mall in forever, actually. The last time I went, I bought this phone case that the kiosk guy swore was completely indestructible, but I dropped it in the parking lot on the way to my car and the screen protector cracked immediately. The parking lot was being repaved too, so it smelled awful, like hot tar and chemicals, and my sneakers got this black sticky stuff on the soles that I still can't scrape off. I tried using a butter knife but it just bent the knife... but wait, sorry, what did you ask? Unusually up? Yeah, no, nothing like that. Just my regular energy.
Do you often find yourself worrying a lot about everyday things?

Worrying? Um, no, not really. I mean, I don't sit around stressing about stuff. Well, except maybe if I'm gonna be late, because I hate being late. But even then, it's not like a big worry. Like this morning, I thought I was gonna be late because my alarm didn't go off. Or maybe it did and I just swiped it off without waking up? I do that sometimes. I had to set my phone across the room for a while, but then I'd just get out of bed, turn it off, and get right back in. My bed is super comfortable though, I got this memory foam topper on sale at Target. Target is dangerous, honestly. You go in for toothpaste and you come out with a throw pillow, three bags of weird flavored chips, and a new lamp. I got these jalapeño popper chips last time that were so spicy I literally couldn't eat more than three. Dave ate the whole bag though, he has a stomach made of iron. We went to this questionable taco truck last week and he got the mystery meat burrito, and he was totally fine. I had a regular chicken taco and I swear my stomach was doing backflips all night. The truck was parked right next to the hospital too, which you'd think would make them more careful about food safety, but I guess not. They had this really cool neon sign though, it was a taco wearing sunglasses... wait, sorry, worrying? No, I don't really worry about everyday things much. Just normal stuff, I guess.

latest_inference.note: Denied generalized worry, making F41.1 less likely. Persistent lifelong hyperactivity/restlessness with tangentiality and no evidence for medication-induced akathisia, psychosis, or mania supports narrowing to ADHD/other specified type.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports a persistent, non-episodic pattern of marked motor restlessness and inability to remain seated, with frequent pacing, shifting, foot tapping, and getting up to move in work and classroom settings over months. Medication-induced akathisia is not supported because the patient denies prescription medication use or dose changes. Core inattentive symptoms since childhood are denied, making classic ADHD presentations less supported, but the interview evidence does support a hyperactivity/restlessness syndrome best captured by other specified hyperkinetic disorder.
